hero.title: Cultivating Progress Through Cooperative Strength
hero.desc: Meki Batu Union stands as a testament to the power of collective farming in Ethiopia. We unite 136 primary cooperatives and 8,471 member farmers to ensure fair trade, sustainable practices, and premium quality produce for domestic and global markets.
hero.imageAlt: Fertile Ethiopian agricultural land during golden hour

item1.heading: Inception in Meki
item1.text: Established in Meki town with 12 primary cooperatives and 527 founding members, pooling 500,000 ETB in initial capital to build a agricultural firm.

item2.heading: Regional Expansion
item2.text: Expanded across six Rift Valley districts in East Shewa and Arsi zones, scaling modern irrigation infrastructure across 6,065.25 hectares of fertile farmland.

item3.heading: 136 Co-ops & 8,471 Farmers
item3.text: Today uniting 136 cooperatives and 8,471 farmers with 154.2 million ETB in union capital, delivering reliable, certified produce across domestic and global markets.

missionVision.visionText: By 2032, we see a strong and competitive union that ensures sustainable benefits for its members and plays a leading role in the regional and national economy.
missionVision.missionText: The socio-economic development of our members is achieved by fulfilling the union's objectives — building community cohesion from grassroots to higher-level structures, strengthening self-confidence, and fostering self-governance and self-help, to secure lasting benefit for union members.
objectives: To empower member farmers through fair market access and equitable trade practices.
To promote and implement sustainable, environmentally conscious agricultural methods.
To provide continuous education and capacity building for rural farming communities.
To maintain the highest standards of produce quality for international export.

governance.title: Governance & Organizational Structure
governance.desc: Democratic member governance ensuring transparent leadership, strict internal control, and professional management from the General Assembly to farm-level cooperatives.
governance.subtitle: Interactive governance chart: select any leadership tier or department to inspect mandate & structure.
governance.teamDesc: Union directors and department heads driving cooperative operations across all member societies.
governance.deptDesc: Division heads managing agronomy, commercial marketing, financial reporting, legal compliance, and human resources.

facilities.title: Operational Facilities & Infrastructure
facilities.desc: Our modern infrastructure enables farm-gate cold preservation, centralized grading, and certified packaging across East Shewa and Arsi zones.

infrastructure.title: Operational Resources
infrastructure.desc: The logistical and technical backbone powering our 136 member cooperatives, from 2,000-tonne cold storage and refrigerated transport fleets to seed conditioning plants and lake pumping stations.

partners.title: Strategic & Institutional Partners
partners.desc: We work closely with government agencies, research institutions, and international development organizations to advance sustainable agriculture.

p1.title: Research & Seed Trials
p1.desc: Partnering with EIAR and OARI to test and multiply high-germination certified seed varieties.

p2.title: Landscape & Sustainability
p2.desc: Collaborating with Wetlands International and IDH on Rift Valley conservation and drip irrigation.

p3.title: Cold-Chain & Logistics
p3.desc: Equipped with ATI refrigerated fleet and pack house precooling to minimize post-harvest loss.

p4.title: Market Access & Off-Taking
p4.desc: Supplying Ethiopian Airlines Inflight Catering, European exporters, and Addis Ababa retail outlets.

partners.civicDesc: Strategic municipal government partners fostering agro-infrastructure, municipal processing centers, watershed protection, and community welfare across the Dembal Lake basin.
